_about: Per-platform limits read by scripts/postcheck.py. Every value was written from memory on the date shown and is unverified: platforms change these without notice, so open the source named and correct the value before posting. An entry with "kind": "guidance" produces a warning; every other entry is treated as a hard limit and produces a failure. Counting methods: 'codepoints' counts Unicode code points; 'weighted' counts code points inside light_ranges as 1 and all others as 2; 'graphemes' counts what a reader sees as one character (approximated: combining marks, joiners, variation selectors and skin-tone modifiers do not count, a flag pair counts once). Where url_chars is set, every link counts as that many characters whatever its real length.

max_chars.source: X developer documentation, 'Counting characters'; applies to accounts without a paid long-post plan

light_ranges.unit: code point ranges that count as 1

max_hashtags.source: X help pages on hashtags (a recommendation, not a limit)

count.source: assumed; LinkedIn does not document how it counts

fold_chars.source: observed behaviour reported by users; varies by device

max_hashtags.source: mstack working value, not a platform rule

max_chars.source: Mastodon documentation, default server setting; each server may set its own

front_matter.source: mstack working set; a site generator may ask for more or other keys

title_max_chars.source: common guidance for when a search result title is cut; no search engine publishes a fixed limit

description_max_chars.source: common guidance for when a search snippet is cut; no search engine publishes a fixed limit
